text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: P1 paging: high tail latency and error rate on inference-llama-mistral-qwen pools (kv-cache growth + continuous batching). Incident auto-created: INC-2419129

pagerduty-bot: Symptoms: sustained p95/p99 request latency spike, KV cache memory growth > 75% on several shards, autoscaler unable to keep up, customer-facing 502/504s for streaming endpoints. Alerting channels: incidents + eng-runtime + eng-sre.

alex: oncall here, acknowledging. pulling metrics now.

sam: I see the KV eviction counter ramping and continuous_batch_queue_depth climbing. Looks like a regression after the 04:00 deploy that changed `continuous_batch_max_bytes` to 4MB.

irina: paging in — can you paste the prometheus queries?

sam: sure, grabbing quick ones:
```
# evictions per shard
sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total{job=\"runtime\"}[1m])) by (shard)

# queue depth
sum(runtime_contbatch_queue_depth)

# p99 latency for model route
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~\"/v1/generate.*\"}[5m])) by (le))
```

alex: thanks. I can see p99 for `mistral-1.2-gqa` went from ~120ms to 1.2s after the change. Llama routes also affected but less so. Qwen seems to thrash when prefetch windows overlap.

maria: Customer impact: multiple enterprise customers reported degraded streaming sessions and truncated outputs. Support ticket numbers: TCK-885, TCK-889. They're seeing mid-generations drop with 502.

jake: flagged for customer comms. Are we sure it's config-only and not model binary?

sam: initial theory: increasing batch size combined with a lazy eviction path in the KV cache causes long tail stall when a large batch hits a shard that needs to rebuild KV entries. MQA routes amplify because they're more stateful per token.

irina: mitigation options: rollback deploy, temp throttle continuous batching, or enable aggressive KV eviction on suspect shards. Which is least risky?

alex: prefer targeted config flip first to avoid full deploy rollback. We can flip `continuous_batch_max_bytes` back to prior 1MB and set `kv_max_memory_mb`=800 for affected pools. Do we have a runbook snippet?

ops-bot: runbook snippet: `runbooks/contbatch-kv-thrash.md` (link)

sam: I'll push the config change to the runtime control plane for `region=us-east, pool=mistral-gqa` and `pool=mistral-mqa` first. Doing a canary on 2 shards.

alex: do the canary, watch p99 and eviction counters for 5 minutes, then expand. If we see immediate improvement, escalate to wider config change.

sam: applying canary now. cURL to control plane:
```bash
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.internal/api/v1/runtime/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"selector":{"pool":"mistral-gqa","region":"us-east"},"overrides":{"continuous_batch_max_bytes":1048576,"kv_max_memory_mb":800}}'
```

sam: canary applied to shards s-12 and s-13. Monitoring...

irina: watching metrics. eviction rate dropping on s-12, queue depth falling by ~30%. p99 down from 1.2s to 210ms on canary shards. :thumbsup:

maria: getting green signal from customers for TCK-885, reports improved streaming continuity. TCK-889 still sporadic.

alex: expand change to all mistral-gqa shards, and mirror to mistral-mqa. Keep qwen/llama untouched for now. Coordination: sam do change, irina watch metrics, jake prep customer notes.

sam: expanding to all mistral-gqa now, then mistral-mqa.

ops-bot: deploy log: cfg-update 2419129999 by sam — applied to 18 shards for mistral-gqa.

irina: p99 across pool now ~190-230ms, eviction rates stabilized, kv memory usage trending down. Autoscaler activity reduced.

jake: updating support tickets: TCK-885 resolved, TCK-889 awaiting final validation. Sending interim customer note: "We've applied a mitigation to reduce latency and dropped error rate; monitoring continues."

maria: any root cause hypothesis for post-deploy regressions? We should capture exact commit.

sam: commit that adjusted batching: `runtime@3a7f2b` — increased continuous batch thresholds to target throughput. That change interacts poorly with LRU lazy-eviction when per-session KV size variance is high. In practice big sessions cause cache rebuilds and block batch consumers.

alex: action items:
- sam: open INC-2419129-PR with config diff and rollback plan (IN PROG)
- irina: postmortem checklist and memory/eviction thresholds to test (IN PROG)
- sam: add a short-term guard: fail open to smaller batches when shard eviction rate > 5/min (DONE as canary?)
- product/maria: coordinate customer follow-up and severity notes (IN PROG)

sam: created PR: https://phabricator.redwood/PR-1842 (link). Includes rollback and metric dashboards.

irina: setting incident severity to SEV2 -> SEV3 as customer errors dropping. Logging timeline for handoff.

alex: oncall handoff in 30m — I'll summarize for next oncall: cause = increased continuous_batch thresholds interacting with lazy KV eviction under heavy MQA/GQA sessions; mitigation = revert batch size & tighten kv memory thresholds; next steps = postmortem + automated guardrails.

maria: can we add a regression test in CI that stresses KV size variance with MQA tokens? I can pick that up with sam.

sam: will add perf test and a Prometheus alert: `kv_cache_evictions_total > 5/m` per shard triggers temp batch throttle.

jake: sending customers final note: "Mitigation applied; we are monitoring and will follow up with RCA."

alex: thanks everyone. If anything regresses ping @alex and @irina. Closing incident channel when next oncall confirms stable for 60m.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2419129 updated: status->mitigated; severity->SEV3; assignees: sam, irina.

ops-bot: archive note: cfg snapshot saved to s3://cfg-backups/2419129999.json

(END OF THREAD)
